title: Flat Tag Identity
summary: make each canonical tag one globally unique name and remove group as data without moving semantic meaning into another registry field
content_html:
Flat Tag Identity

Result

A canonical tag is one globally unique normalized name such as moss. subject:moss, a singular group, a groups array, allowed-group policy, and group-derived analytical behavior are not part of the tag model.

Assignments and aliases refer directly to the flat tag_id. Interpretative meaning belongs in the tag's document after Tag-document linking; this feature does not replace group with another classification field.

Why this is separate

Flattening identity changes canonical registry keys and every assignment and alias that refers to them. It also requires human decisions where the same label currently appears in more than one group. That is a coherent vocabulary migration, not part of document association or report filtering.

The existing registry description remains available through this feature so Tag-document linking can use it as one-time seed content. Removing that field before the documents exist would discard the current semantic source.

Feature Documents

  • Flat Tag Identity Concept — the lasting identity and ownership model.
  • Flat Tag Identity Delivery — the proposed complete schema, data, service, and UI migration.

Boundary

  • Tag Vocabulary Import Retirement removes obsolete bulk paths before this feature changes canonical identity.
  • This feature owns flat IDs, manual collision decisions, reference migration, and removal of group-dependent executable behavior.
  • It does not create or associate documents, remove registry descriptions, or implement semantic-token targets.
  • Tag-document linking follows this feature and establishes the required registry-to-document relationship.

Durable Destinations

Shipped identity and source ownership belong in Tag Source Data, Tag Registry, and Tag Aliases. Assignment consequences belong in Series Tags and Series Tag Editor.
